objects.description: Enumeration controlling how alpha is handled when rendering pixbufs; currently bilevel mask vs. placeholder for full alpha (deprecated).
Enumeration of supported color spaces for pixbuf data; currently only RGB is supported.

objects.definition: typedef struct _GdkPixbuf GdkPixbuf;
objects.description: Opaque image data object representing a pixel buffer with optional alpha; reference-counted GObject type. Full structure is not defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef void (* GdkPixbufDestroyNotify) (guchar *pixels, gpointer data);
objects.description: Callback type used to free pixel memory supplied to gdk_pixbuf_new_from_data; called with the pixel pointer and user data when the pixbuf is finalized.
Error codes for the GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR domain used by pixbuf loading/saving/processing APIs.

objects.definition:
typedef gboolean (*GdkPixbufSaveFunc)   (const gchar *buf,
					 gsize count,
					 GError **error,
					 gpointer data);
objects.description: Callback type used by save-to-callback APIs; receives successive byte chunks to write and reports errors via GError.

Enumeration of interpolation filters used by GdkPixbuf scaling/compositing APIs. Values select quality/speed trade-offs; HYPER is deprecated in favor of BILINEAR. Used as a parameter in scaling functions.
Enumeration specifying discrete rotation angles (in degrees) for gdk_pixbuf_rotate_simple(). The numeric values match the angle in degrees.

GObject-derived base type representing an image animation in gdk-pixbuf. The instance struct contains only the GObject parent; behavior is provided by its class vfuncs in GdkPixbufAnimationClass. Deprecated for loading/animating assets since 2.44.

Class vtable for GdkPixbufAnimation. Backends subclass this and implement the virtual methods to provide animation behavior: reporting static-image-ness, returning a representative static frame, frame size, and creating an iterator starting from a given time.
GObject-derived iterator over frames of a GdkPixbufAnimation. The instance struct stores only the GObject parent; behavior is provided by GdkPixbufAnimationIterClass vfuncs. Deprecated since 2.44.
Class vtable for GdkPixbufAnimationIter. Backends implement timing of frames, current frame retrieval, status of loading, and advancement to a given time.

objects.definition: typedef struct _GdkPixbufSimpleAnim GdkPixbufSimpleAnim;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a simple, frame-based animation in GdkPixbuf. The concrete struct layout is hidden; instances are GObject-based and represent a sequence of pixbuf frames with a playback rate and optional looping.

objects.definition: typedef struct _GdkPixbufSimpleAnimClass GdkPixbufSimpleAnimClass;
objects.description: Opaque GObject class structure for GdkPixbufSimpleAnim. Defines the class/type information and virtual methods for the simple animation type. Actual fields are not exposed in this header.

Opaque-ish record describing an image format supported by a gdk-pixbuf loader module. Applications should not access fields directly; modules fill it to advertise format metadata such as name, description, MIME types, extensions, capability flags, disabled state, and license. The signature field points to an array of magic-patterns used for sniffing.

Pattern element used in a loader’s signature for magic-number matching. Each entry provides a byte prefix, an optional mask with special characters controlling matching semantics, and a relevance score. Arrays are terminated with an entry whose prefix is NULL.

Vtable and metadata holder for a gdk-pixbuf loader backend. Populated at module load time to provide load/save entry points and references to its GdkPixbufFormat info. Not thread-safety or lifetime documented here; typically created/managed by the module loader. The reserved slots are for future ABI. Fields point to function typedefs declared in this header.

GObject-derived progressive image loader used to incrementally feed image data (by type or MIME) and obtain a GdkPixbuf or animation as it becomes available. Internals are private; treat as an opaque GObject instance.

The class/virtual function table for GdkPixbufLoader. Subclasses can override signals/callbacks for progressive loading events (size prepared, area prepared/updated, and closed). Intended for type implementers rather than applications.

No new typedef or enum for GType is defined here; this entry is not applicable and should be ignored. Note: All other referenced types (GdkPixbuf, GdkPixbufAnimation, GdkPixbufFormat, GObject, GObjectClass, gpointer, guchar, gsize, GBytes, gboolean, GError) are declared in other headers and are not defined here.

Deprecated enum (since 2.32) containing flag bits for GdkPixdata: color type (RGB/RGBA), sample width (currently 8-bit), and encoding (raw or RLE). Values are bitfields intended to be combined in pixdata_type. Note that although an enum is used, it serves as a flags bitmask.

Opaque-ish struct representing serialized/inlined pixel data used by gdk-pixbuf utilities. Fields include a magic number, total length, type flags (GdkPixdataType), dimensions, rowstride, and a pointer to pixel data. Deprecated since 2.32; still used by helper functions to (de)serialize or convert to/from GdkPixbuf.

Deprecated enum (since 2.32) of options for generating C source from GdkPixdata via gdk_pixdata_to_csource(). The first trio selects output form (stream, struct, or macros), GTYPES/CTYPES choose type style, and remaining bits add static/const qualifiers and include an RLE decoder macro.

Opaque integral type used by GLib’s GObject type system to identify registered types. This header only declares functions returning GType for various enums; it does not define any enums or new types itself.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_error_quark
functions.description: Returns the GQuark identifying the GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR domain for GError. Use it to check or create GErrors produced by gdk-pixbuf operations.
requirements: None beyond standard GLib: call at any time; thread-safe to call multiple times.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for GdkPixbuf. Useful for runtime type checks and GObject introspection/registration.
requirements: May be called at any time; returns a stable type id.
Function is const (no side effects).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_ref
functions.description: Deprecated: use g_object_ref(). Increments the reference count of a GdkPixbuf and returns the same pointer.
requirements: pixbuf must be a valid, initialized GdkPixbuf.
Do not mix ref/unref with manual freeing; lifetime is managed via reference counting.
Prefer g_object_ref().

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_unref
functions.description: Deprecated: use g_object_unref(). Decrements the reference count of a GdkPixbuf, freeing it when it reaches zero.
requirements: pixbuf must be a valid, initialized GdkPixbuf (not already finalized).
After unref, do not use pixbuf unless you still hold another reference.
Prefer g_object_unref().

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_colorspace
functions.description: Returns the colorspace of the pixbuf. Currently only GDK_COLORSPACE_RGB is supported.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_n_channels
functions.description: Returns the number of channels per pixel (e.g., 3 for RGB, 4 for RGBA).
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_has_alpha
functions.description: Returns whether the pixbuf has an alpha channel.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_bits_per_sample
functions.description: Returns the number of bits per color sample in the pixbuf.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_pixels
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the raw pixel buffer for the pixbuf. The data is in row-major order with rowstride given by gdk_pixbuf_get_rowstride().
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
The returned pointer remains valid while the pixbuf is alive; do not free it.
Modifying the returned buffer modifies the pixbuf; ensure the pixbuf is not shared if you mutate.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_width
functions.description: Returns the width of the pixbuf in pixels.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_height
functions.description: Returns the height of the pixbuf in pixels.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_rowstride
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes between rows (the rowstride) of the pixbuf.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_byte_length
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the pixel data buffer for the pixbuf.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_pixels_with_length
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the raw pixel buffer and writes its total length in bytes into length.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the size.
The returned pointer remains valid while the pixbuf is alive; do not free it.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_read_pixels
functions.description: Returns a read-only pointer to the raw pixel data of the pixbuf.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
Do not modify or free the returned data; validity is tied to the lifetime of pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_read_pixel_bytes
functions.description: Returns a GBytes wrapping the pixbuf’s pixel data for read-only access and safe sharing.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
The returned GBytes must be unreffed by the caller when no longer needed.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new (GdkColorspace colorspace, gboolean has_alpha, int bits_per_sample, int width, int height);
functions.description: Creates a new blank pixbuf with an automatically chosen rowstride and newly allocated pixel buffer.
requirements: colorspace must be a supported value (currently GDK_COLORSPACE_RGB).
width and height should be positive integers.
bits_per_sample must be a supported value for gdk-pixbuf (usually 8; other values may not be supported).
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_calculate_rowstride
functions.signature: gint gdk_pixbuf_calculate_rowstride (GdkColorspace colorspace, gboolean has_alpha, int bits_per_sample, int width, int height);
functions.description: Calculates an optimal rowstride (bytes per row) for an image with the given format and dimensions.
requirements: colorspace must be a supported value (currently GDK_COLORSPACE_RGB).
width and height should be non-negative; realistic positive values are expected.
bits_per_sample must be a value supported by gdk-pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_copy
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of the given pixbuf, duplicating its pixel data and options.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_subpixbuf
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_subpixbuf (GdkPixbuf *src_pixbuf, int src_x, int src_y, int width, int height);
functions.description: Creates a new pixbuf that references a rectangular subregion of another pixbuf without copying pixels.
requirements: src_pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
The rectangle (src_x, src_y, width, height) must lie entirely within src_pixbuf’s bounds.
The lifetime of the new pixbuf is tied to src_pixbuf’s pixel data; keep src_pixbuf alive while using the subpixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_file
functions.description: Loads an image from a file into a new GdkPixbuf using built-in loader modules.
requirements: filename must be a valid, non-NULL path to an image file.
On failure, returns NULL and sets error in the GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR or G_FILE_ERROR domain; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.
The caller must unref the returned pixbuf when done.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_file_at_size
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_from_file_at_size (const char *filename, int width, int height, GError **error);
functions.description: Loads an image from file and scales it to the requested size, preserving aspect ratio according to loader behavior.
requirements: filename must be a valid, non-NULL path.
width and height specify desired dimensions; values should be positive.
On failure, returns NULL and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.
The caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_file_at_scale
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_from_file_at_scale (const char *filename, int width, int height, gboolean preserve_aspect_ratio, GError **error);
functions.description: Loads an image from file and scales to the requested size, optionally preserving aspect ratio.
requirements: filename must be a valid, non-NULL path.
width and height specify desired dimensions; values should be positive.
If error is provided, it must point to NULL on entry; returns NULL on failure with error set.
The caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_resource
functions.description: Loads an image from a GResource path into a new GdkPixbuf.
requirements: resource_path must be a valid, non-NULL resource path registered in the process.
On failure, returns NULL and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.
Caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_resource_at_scale
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_from_resource_at_scale (const char *resource_path, int width, int height, gboolean preserve_aspect_ratio, GError **error);
functions.description: Loads an image from a GResource and scales it to the requested size, optionally preserving aspect ratio.
requirements: resource_path must be non-NULL and refer to a valid resource.
width and height specify desired dimensions; values should be positive.
If error is provided, it must point to NULL on entry; returns NULL on failure with error set.
Caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_data
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_from_data (const guchar *data, GdkColorspace colorspace, gboolean has_alpha, int bits_per_sample, int width, int height, int rowstride, GdkPixbufDestroyNotify destroy_fn, gpointer destroy_fn_data);
functions.description: Creates a pixbuf that uses the provided pixel data buffer without copying. A destroy notify may be provided to free or finalize the data when the pixbuf is finalized.
requirements: data must point to a pixel buffer large enough for the specified dimensions and rowstride.
colorspace must be supported (currently GDK_COLORSPACE_RGB).
width and height should be positive; rowstride must be at least the number of bytes per row for the given format.
If provided, destroy_fn will be called with pixels and destroy_fn_data when the pixbuf is finalized; it may be NULL if no special cleanup is needed.
The data must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_bytes
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_from_bytes (GBytes *data, GdkColorspace colorspace, gboolean has_alpha, int bits_per_sample, int width, int height, int rowstride);
functions.description: Creates a pixbuf that references pixel data stored in a GBytes without copying. The GBytes keeps the memory alive.
requirements: data must be a non-NULL GBytes containing a buffer large enough for the specified image layout.
colorspace must be supported (currently GDK_COLORSPACE_RGB).
width and height should be positive; rowstride must be compatible with the format.
The caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_xpm_data
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a pixbuf from inline XPM data.
requirements: data must be a valid XPM data array terminated according to the XPM format.
Returns NULL on failure. Prefer modern image formats and loaders.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_inline
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_from_inline (gint data_length, const guint8 *data, gboolean copy_pixels, GError **error);
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a pixbuf from inline-embedded image data as produced by gdk-pixbuf-csource.
requirements: data must point to valid inline image data; data_length is its size in bytes.
If copy_pixels is FALSE, the data must remain valid for the lifetime of the pixbuf.
On failure, returns NULL and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_fill
functions.description: Fills the entire pixbuf with a solid color given as a packed 32-bit pixel value (channel layout depends on pixbuf format).
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and writable (not shared/immutable).
If pixbuf has no alpha, the alpha component of pixel is ignored.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_save (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, const char *filename, const char *type, GError **error, ...);
functions.description: Saves the pixbuf to a file of the given image type. Optional key–value pairs can be provided as varargs to control save options.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
filename must be a valid, writable path.
type must name a supported image format (e.g., "png", "jpeg").
Varargs, if provided, must be NULL-terminated pairs: (const char* key, const char* value, ... , NULL).
Returns FALSE on failure and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_savev
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_savev (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, const char *filename, const char *type, char **option_keys, char **option_values, GError **error);
functions.description: Saves the pixbuf to a file with the given type, passing save options via arrays of keys and values.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
filename must be a valid, writable path.
type must name a supported image format.
option_keys and option_values, if non-NULL, should be arrays of strings of equal length and NULL-terminated (per GLib conventions).
Returns FALSE on failure and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_callback
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_save_to_callback (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, GdkPixbufSaveFunc save_func, gpointer user_data, const char *type, GError **error, ...);
functions.description: Encodes the pixbuf to the specified image type and writes the bytes via a user-provided callback. Optional key–value save options can be provided as varargs.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
save_func must be a valid function that returns TRUE on success and sets error on failure.
type must name a supported image format.
Varargs, if provided, must be NULL-terminated key/value pairs.
On failure returns FALSE and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_callbackv
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_save_to_callbackv (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, GdkPixbufSaveFunc save_func, gpointer user_data, const char *type, char **option_keys, char **option_values, GError **error);
functions.description: Encodes the pixbuf and writes via a callback, passing save options as arrays of keys/values.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
save_func must be non-NULL and follow the GdkPixbufSaveFunc contract (return TRUE on success; on failure set error and return FALSE).
type must name a supported image format.
option_keys and option_values, if provided, should be arrays of equal length and NULL-terminated (GLib convention).
On failure returns FALSE and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_buffer
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_save_to_buffer (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, gchar **buffer, gsize *buffer_size, const char *type, GError **error, ...);
functions.description: Encodes the pixbuf to the given image type and returns a newly allocated memory buffer containing the encoded data.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
buffer and buffer_size must be non-NULL; on success, *buffer is allocated and must be freed with g_free(), and *buffer_size set to its length.
type must name a supported image format.
Varargs, if provided, must be NULL-terminated key/value pairs.
Returns FALSE on failure and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_bufferv
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_save_to_bufferv (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, gchar **buffer, gsize *buffer_size, const char *type, char **option_keys, char **option_values, GError **error);
functions.description: Encodes the pixbuf to a memory buffer, passing save options as arrays of keys/values.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
buffer and buffer_size must be non-NULL; on success, *buffer is allocated and must be freed with g_free().
type must name a supported image format.
option_keys and option_values, if provided, should be arrays of equal length and NULL-terminated (GLib convention).
Returns FALSE on failure and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream
functions.description: Synchronously loads an image from a GInputStream into a new pixbuf.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable GInputStream positioned at the start of image data.
cancellable may be NULL; if non-NULL it can be used to cancel the operation.
On failure returns NULL and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.
Caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_async
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_async (GInputStream *stream, GCancellable *cancellable, GAsyncReadyCallback callback, gpointer user_data);
functions.description: Starts asynchronously loading an image from a GInputStream. Completion is reported to the callback; retrieve the result with gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_finish().
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable GInputStream that remains valid for the duration of the async operation.
callback may be NULL if the caller will otherwise observe completion; typically non-NULL.
cancellable may be NULL; if non-NULL it may be used to cancel.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_finish
functions.description: Finishes an async load started by gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_async() and returns the loaded pixbuf, or NULL on error.
requirements: async_result must be the GAsyncResult from the corresponding async call.
On failure returns NULL and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.
Caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_at_scale
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_at_scale (GInputStream *stream, gint width, gint height, gboolean preserve_aspect_ratio, GCancellable *cancellable, GError **error);
functions.description: Synchronously loads an image from a stream and scales it to the requested size, optionally preserving aspect ratio.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable GInputStream.
width and height specify desired dimensions; values should be positive.
cancellable may be NULL; if non-NULL it can be used to cancel.
On failure returns NULL and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_at_scale_async
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_at_scale_async (GInputStream *stream, gint width, gint height, gboolean preserve_aspect_ratio, GCancellable *cancellable, GAsyncReadyCallback callback, gpointer user_data);
functions.description: Starts asynchronously loading and scaling an image from a stream. Complete with gdk_pixbuf_new_from_stream_finish().
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable GInputStream that remains valid for the duration of the async operation.
width and height specify desired dimensions; values should be positive.
callback should be provided to receive completion; cancellable may be NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, GOutputStream *stream, const char *type, GCancellable *cancellable, GError **error, ...);
functions.description: Synchronously encodes the pixbuf into the given image type and writes the data to a GOutputStream. Optional key–value save options can be provided as varargs.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
stream must be a valid, writable GOutputStream.
type must name a supported image format.
Varargs, if provided, must be NULL-terminated key/value pairs.
Returns FALSE on failure and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream_async
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream_async (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, GOutputStream *stream, const gchar *type, GCancellable *cancellable, GAsyncReadyCallback callback, gpointer user_data, ...);
functions.description: Starts asynchronously encoding and writing the pixbuf to a GOutputStream. Optional key–value save options can be provided as varargs. Complete with gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream_finish().
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
stream must be a valid, writable GOutputStream and remain valid for the duration of the async operation.
type must name a supported image format.
Varargs, if provided, must be NULL-terminated key/value pairs.
Provide a callback to receive completion; cancellable may be NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream_finish
functions.description: Completes an async save started by gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream_async(). Returns TRUE on success.
requirements: async_result must be from the matching async save call.
On failure returns FALSE and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_streamv_async
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_save_to_streamv_async (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, GOutputStream *stream, const gchar *type, gchar **option_keys, gchar **option_values, GCancellable *cancellable, GAsyncReadyCallback callback, gpointer user_data);
functions.description: Starts asynchronously encoding and writing the pixbuf to a stream, passing save options via arrays of keys/values. Complete with gdk_pixbuf_save_to_stream_finish().
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
stream must be a valid, writable GOutputStream and remain valid for the async duration.
type must name a supported image format.
option_keys and option_values, if provided, should be arrays of equal length and NULL-terminated (GLib convention).
Provide a callback to receive completion; cancellable may be NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_save_to_streamv
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_save_to_streamv (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, GOutputStream *stream, const char *type, char **option_keys, char **option_values, GCancellable *cancellable, GError **error);
functions.description: Synchronously encodes and writes a pixbuf to a stream, passing save options via arrays of keys/values.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
stream must be a valid, writable GOutputStream.
type must name a supported image format.
option_keys and option_values, if provided, should be arrays of equal length and NULL-terminated (GLib convention).
Returns FALSE on failure and sets error; if error is non-NULL it must point to NULL.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_add_alpha
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_add_alpha (const GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, gboolean substitute_color, guchar r, guchar g, guchar b);
functions.description: Returns a copy of pixbuf with an alpha channel. If substitute_color is TRUE, pixels matching the specified RGB color will be made fully transparent.
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
r, g, b are 8-bit channel values for the color to make transparent when substitute_color is TRUE.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must unref the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_copy_area
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_copy_area (const GdkPixbuf *src_pixbuf, int src_x, int src_y, int width, int height, GdkPixbuf *dest_pixbuf, int dest_x, int dest_y);
functions.description: Copies a rectangular region from src_pixbuf into dest_pixbuf at the specified destination coordinates.
requirements: src_pixbuf and dest_pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
The source rectangle must be fully within src_pixbuf bounds.
The destination rectangle (dest_x..dest_x+width, dest_y..dest_y+height) must be within dest_pixbuf bounds.
Behavior is undefined if src and dest are the same pixbuf with overlapping regions.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_saturate_and_pixelate
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_saturate_and_pixelate (const GdkPixbuf *src, GdkPixbuf *dest, gfloat saturation, gboolean pixelate);
functions.description: Adjusts saturation of src into dest and optionally applies a pixelation effect. Useful for creating dimmed/highlighted thumbnails.
requirements: src and dest must be non-NULL, initialized pixbufs of the same dimensions.
saturation is a floating-point factor; extreme values may clamp according to implementation.
dest must be writable.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_apply_embedded_orientation
functions.description: Returns a new pixbuf transformed according to the image’s embedded orientation metadata (e.g., EXIF), if present.
requirements: src must be non-NULL and initialized.
Returns a new pixbuf (caller must unref) which may equal a copy if no orientation is present.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_set_option
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixbuf_set_option (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, const gchar *key, const gchar *value);
functions.description: Attaches a key/value option pair to the pixbuf (e.g., metadata used by savers).
requirements: pixbuf must be non-NULL and initialized.
key and value must be non-NULL strings.
Returns FALSE if the option cannot be set for this pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_option

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_remove_option

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_options

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_copy_options

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_scale
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_scale (const GdkPixbuf *src, GdkPixbuf *dest, int dest_x, int dest_y, int dest_width, int dest_height, double offset_x, double offset_y, double scale_x, double scale_y, GdkInterpType interp_type);
functions.description: Scales a source GdkPixbuf into a specified rectangle of a destination GdkPixbuf, using the given interpolation method. The scaling is defined by scale and offset parameters (an affine transform limited to scale+translate). Use when you need to render a resized view of src into a sub-rectangle of dest.
requirements: src must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest_x and dest_y specify the top-left destination pixel where scaling output begins; dest_width and dest_height specify the size of the target region in dest and should be non-negative integers.
interp_type must be a valid GdkInterpType enumerator.

offset_x and offset_y, together with scale_x and scale_y, define the transformation from destination to source coordinates; typical usage uses positive, non-zero scale factors (exact constraints are not documented here).
The specified destination rectangle [dest_x..dest_x+dest_width), [dest_y..dest_y+dest_height) should lie within dest’s bounds to avoid out-of-bounds writes.
Both pixbufs must follow gdk-pixbuf’s standard format (8-bit samples); no conversion is performed by this call.
This function does not return a value; callers must ensure parameters are valid to avoid runtime warnings or crashes.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_composite
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_composite (const GdkPixbuf *src, GdkPixbuf *dest, int dest_x, int dest_y, int dest_width, int dest_height, double offset_x, double offset_y, double scale_x, double scale_y, GdkInterpType interp_type, int overall_alpha);
functions.description: Scales src and composites it over a rectangle in dest with an additional overall alpha factor, using the specified interpolation. Use when overlaying a (possibly scaled) pixbuf onto another with global opacity control.
requirements: src must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest_x, dest_y, dest_width, dest_height define the destination rectangle; dest_width and dest_height should be non-negative integers.
interp_type must be a valid GdkInterpType enumerator.
overall_alpha is an integer opacity factor typically in the 0..255 range (0 fully transparent, 255 fully opaque); callers should clamp inputs accordingly.
The destination rectangle should be within dest’s bounds to avoid out-of-bounds writes.
offset_x/offset_y and scale_x/scale_y define the mapping from destination to source; typical usage uses positive scale (exact constraints are not documented here).
Both pixbufs must use gdk-pixbuf’s standard pixel format (8-bit samples).
This function returns no value; callers must validate arguments and handle any library warnings/errors appropriately.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_composite_color
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_composite_color (const GdkPixbuf *src, GdkPixbuf *dest, int dest_x, int dest_y, int dest_width, int dest_height, double offset_x, double offset_y, double scale_x, double scale_y, GdkInterpType interp_type, int overall_alpha, int check_x, int check_y, int check_size, guint32 color1, guint32 color2);
functions.description: Scales src and composites it over a checkboard pattern painted into a rectangle of dest. The check pattern is defined by check_x/y offsets, a tile size, and two colors. Useful for compositing over a transparency-indicating background.
requirements: src must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest_x, dest_y, dest_width, dest_height define the destination rectangle; dest_width and dest_height should be non-negative integers.
interp_type must be a valid GdkInterpType enumerator.
overall_alpha is a global opacity factor typically in the 0..255 range; callers should clamp to that range.
check_size should be a positive integer to define square tile size for the check pattern.
check_x and check_y specify the phase/offset of the check pattern in pixels (integers).

color1 and color2 are 32-bit packed colors; the exact channel layout/encoding is not documented in this header and should be consulted in the official gdk-pixbuf documentation before use (unknown here).
The destination rectangle should be within dest’s bounds to avoid out-of-bounds writes.
This function does not return a value; callers must ensure valid parameters.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_scale_simple
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_scale_simple (const GdkPixbuf *src, int dest_width, int dest_height, GdkInterpType interp_type);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new pixbuf containing src scaled to the given width and height using the specified interpolation. Use for straightforward scaling when you don’t need to composite into an existing pixbuf.
requirements: src must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest_width and dest_height should be non-negative integers; zero or negative sizes are invalid for creating a meaningful result.
interp_type must be a valid GdkInterpType enumerator.
On success, the caller owns a new GdkPixbuf reference and must unref it (g_object_unref) when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_composite_color_simple
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf *gdk_pixbuf_composite_color_simple (const GdkPixbuf *src, int dest_width, int dest_height, GdkInterpType interp_type, int overall_alpha, int check_size, guint32 color1, guint32 color2);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new pixbuf with src scaled to the given size, composited over a checkboard pattern defined by check_size and two colors, using the specified interpolation and overall alpha. Use when you need an image over a transparency-style background in one step.
requirements: src must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
dest_width and dest_height should be non-negative integers; zero or negative sizes are invalid for creating a meaningful result.
interp_type must be a valid GdkInterpType enumerator.
overall_alpha is typically in the 0..255 range; callers should clamp accordingly.
check_size should be a positive integer to produce a valid check pattern.
color1 and color2 are 32-bit packed colors; exact channel layout/encoding is not specified in this header (unknown here)—consult official docs.
On success, the caller owns a new GdkPixbuf reference and must unref it (g_object_unref) when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_rotate_simple
functions.description: Returns a new pixbuf with src rotated by the specified right-angle increment (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees). Use for simple, lossless quarter-turn rotations.
requirements: src must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
angle must be one of the GdkPixbufRotation enum values.
On success, the caller owns a new GdkPixbuf reference and must unref it (g_object_unref) when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_flip
functions.description: Returns a new pixbuf which is a flipped (mirrored) version of src. If horizontal is TRUE, the image is flipped horizontally; if FALSE, it is flipped vertically. Use for mirroring images along one axis.
requirements: src must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf.
horizontal must be a valid gboolean (TRUE for horizontal flip, FALSE for vertical flip).
On success, the caller owns a new GdkPixbuf reference and must unref it (g_object_unref) when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for GdkPixbufAnimation. Used for runtime type checks and GObject type registration. Deprecated status does not apply to this function.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_file
functions.description: Loads an animated image from a filesystem path and returns it as a GdkPixbufAnimation. Deprecated since 2.44; prefer a different image loading library for animatable assets.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL, valid path to a readable file containing an image/animation format supported by gdk-pixbuf.
On failure, the function returns NULL and sets a GError; if error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream
functions.description: Loads an animation from a GInputStream and returns a GdkPixbufAnimation. cancellable can be used to cancel the operation. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: stream must be a non-NULL, readable GInputStream positioned at the start of the image data.
cancellable may be NULL or a valid GCancellable.
On failure, the function returns NULL and sets a GError; if error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream_async
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream_async(GInputStream *stream, GCancellable *cancellable, GAsyncReadyCallback callback, gpointer user_data);
functions.description: Asynchronously begins loading an animation from a GInputStream. Completion is reported via callback; obtain the result with gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream_finish. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: stream must be a non-NULL, readable GInputStream positioned at the start of the image data.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream_finish
functions.description: Finishes an asynchronous animation load started with gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream_async and returns the resulting GdkPixbufAnimation. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: async_result must be the GAsyncResult provided to the GAsyncReadyCallback of a prior matching gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream_async call.
On failure, the function returns NULL and sets a GError; if error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_resource
functions.description: Loads an animation from a compiled-in GResource at resource_path and returns a GdkPixbufAnimation. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: resource_path must be a non-NULL resource path present in the process’s GResource (typically starting with '/').
On failure, the function returns NULL and sets a GError; if error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a GdkPixbufAnimation and returns the same pointer. Deprecated in favor of g_object_ref.
requirements: animation must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimation instance.
Each successful ref should be matched with a corresponding unref to avoid leaks.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a GdkPixbufAnimation, possibly finalizing it. Deprecated in favor of g_object_unref.
requirements: animation must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimation instance.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_get_width
functions.description: Returns the frame width, in pixels, of the animation. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: animation must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimation instance.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_get_height
functions.description: Returns the frame height, in pixels, of the animation. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: animation must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimation instance.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_is_static_image
functions.description: Returns whether the animation is effectively a static image (i.e., has a single non-animating frame). Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: animation must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimation instance.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_get_static_image
functions.description: Returns a still GdkPixbuf representing the animation (for static or preview use). Deprecated since 2.44. Ownership/transfer details are not stated in the header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: animation must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimation instance.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_get_iter
functions.description: Creates and returns an iterator to drive playback of the animation, with timing based on start_time. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: animation must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimation instance.
start_time must point to a valid GTimeVal structure; NULL-acceptance is not stated in this header and is therefore unknown.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_iter_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for GdkPixbufAnimationIter. Used for runtime type checks and GObject type registration. Deprecated status does not apply to this function.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_iter_get_delay_time
functions.description: Returns the time in milliseconds that the current frame should be shown. Deprecated since 2.44.
requirements: iter must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbufAnimationIter instance.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_iter_get_pixbuf

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_animation_iter_on_currently_loading_frame

current_time must point to a valid GTimeVal structure; NULL-acceptance is not stated in this header and is therefore unknown.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_non_anim_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for the non-animated animation wrapper type GdkPixbufNonAnim. Available when GDK_PIXBUF_ENABLE_BACKEND is defined.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_non_anim_new
functions.description: Creates a GdkPixbufAnimation that wraps a static GdkPixbuf (i.e., a non-animated animation). Deprecated since 2.44. Ownership of pixbuf and transfer semantics of the return value are not stated in the header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: pixbuf must be a non-NULL, valid GdkPixbuf instance.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_simple_anim_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for the GdkPixbufSimpleAnim class so it can be used with the GObject type system (e.g., for type checks and casting). Typical usage is internal to GObject-based code or when registering/inspecting types.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_simple_anim_iter_get_type

requirements: No preconditions; may be called at any time after the type system is initialized.
Thread-safety follows GLib type system guarantees.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_simple_anim_new
functions.signature: GdkPixbufSimpleAnim *gdk_pixbuf_simple_anim_new (gint width, gint height, gfloat rate);
functions.description: Creates a new simple, frame-based animation with a fixed frame size (width × height) and a playback rate (frames per second). Deprecated since 2.44; prefer newer GdkPixbufAnimation APIs. Caller receives a reference to the new object and should unref it when done.
requirements: animation object is newly created; caller owns the initial reference and must call g_object_unref() when no longer needed (inferred from GObject conventions).
width should be a positive integer (inferred from being pixel dimensions).
height should be a positive integer (inferred from being pixel dimensions).
rate should be a positive floating-point value representing frames per second (inferred from the parameter name and typical animation semantics).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_simple_anim_add_frame
functions.description: Appends a frame to the simple animation. The frame image is provided as a GdkPixbuf. Deprecated since 2.44; prefer newer GdkPixbufAnimation APIs. Ownership transfer of the pixbuf is not specified in this header (unknown).
requirements: animation must be a valid, initialized GdkPixbufSimpleAnim instance (non-NULL).
pixbuf must be a valid GdkPixbuf (non-NULL).

Thread-safety not guaranteed; calls should be made from the same thread that manages the object unless otherwise documented (general GObject practice, inferred).
Ownership/retention of pixbuf by the animation is unknown from this header; callers should not assume it is safe to unref or not unref without consulting full library docs (unknown).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_simple_anim_set_loop

requirements: animation must be a valid, initialized GdkPixbufSimpleAnim instance (non-NULL).
loop must be a valid gboolean value (0/1 or FALSE/TRUE).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_simple_anim_get_loop
functions.description: Returns whether the animation is configured to loop when it reaches the last frame. Deprecated since 2.44; prefer newer GdkPixbufAnimation APIs.
requirements: animation must be a valid, initialized GdkPixbufSimpleAnim instance (non-NULL).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_init_modules
functions.description: Initializes gdk-pixbuf image loader modules from the specified path and makes them available to the library. Typically used by the library’s own initialization code rather than by applications.

Thread-safety or call-order requirements are not documented in this header and are unknown

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for GdkPixbufFormat so it can be used with the GLib type system (e.g., in properties, signals, or runtime type checks).

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_formats
functions.description: Returns a GSList of available image format descriptors (GdkPixbufFormat*) known to gdk-pixbuf at runtime.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_get_name

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_get_description

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_get_mime_types

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_get_extensions

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_is_save_option_supported

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_is_writable

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_is_scalable

Returns TRUE if scalable; FALSE otherwise

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_is_disabled

Returns TRUE if disabled; FALSE otherwise

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_set_disabled

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_get_license

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_get_file_info

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_format_copy

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for GdkPixbufLoader. Used for runtime type checks and GObject introspection/registration.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_new
functions.description: Creates a new progressive image loader that can accept incoming image data in chunks and incrementally construct a GdkPixbuf (or animation). Use gdk_pixbuf_loader_write() or gdk_pixbuf_loader_write_bytes() to feed data, and gdk_pixbuf_loader_close() to finish.

error may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should point to a location initialized to NULL and will be set on failure.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_set_size
functions.signature: void gdk_pixbuf_loader_set_size (GdkPixbufLoader *loader, int width, int height);
functions.description: Hints the desired size (in pixels) for the loaded image. Some loaders may scale the image to these dimensions during loading. This should be called before any data is written to the loader to have effect; after writing begins, behavior is loader-dependent.

buf must be a non-NULL pointer to at least count bytes of readable memory; data must be provided in correct order for the image format.

Must eventually call gdk_pixbuf_loader_close() after the final write to finish loading.
If the function returns FALSE, error (if non-NULL) is set; callers should stop writing further data, handle the error, and close/free the loader.
error may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should point to a location initialized to NULL and will be set on failure.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_write_bytes
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of image data wrapped in a GBytes to the loader. Equivalent to write() but uses GBytes for ownership convenience. Returns TRUE on success; FALSE and sets error on failure.
requirements: loader must be a valid, non-NULL GdkPixbufLoader* not yet closed.
buffer must be a non-NULL GBytes containing the next bytes of the image stream; it must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Can be called multiple times as data arrives; data must be supplied in order for the image format.
Must call gdk_pixbuf_loader_close() after the final write to complete loading.
If the function returns FALSE, error (if non-NULL) is set; callers should stop writing more data, handle the error, and close/free the loader.
error may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should point to a location initialized to NULL and will be set on failure.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_get_pixbuf
functions.description: Returns the current GdkPixbuf being constructed by the loader, or NULL if not yet available (e.g., before the image header is parsed). The returned pixbuf is owned by the loader and may be updated as more data is written; add a reference if you need to keep it beyond the loader’s lifetime.
requirements: loader must be a valid, non-NULL GdkPixbufLoader*.
May return NULL until enough data has been read to create a pixbuf (typically after area_prepared).
Do not assume the contents are final until gdk_pixbuf_loader_close() succeeds.
If you need to keep the pixbuf after unreffing the loader, call g_object_ref() on the returned pixbuf.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_get_animation
functions.description: Returns the GdkPixbufAnimation being constructed, if the data represents an animation (e.g., GIF), or a non-animated, single-frame animation object otherwise; may return NULL if unavailable yet. The returned object is owned by the loader; add a reference if keeping it after the loader. Note: this function is deprecated in newer versions.
requirements: loader must be a valid, non-NULL GdkPixbufLoader*.
May return NULL until enough data has been read to determine/construct the animation.
Ownership remains with the loader; call g_object_ref() if you need to keep it after the loader is unreffed.
Content may change until gdk_pixbuf_loader_close() completes successfully.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_close
functions.description: Indicates that no more data will be written and finalizes image loading. Ensures any pending data is processed and the pixbuf/animation is completed. Returns TRUE on success; on failure returns FALSE and sets error.
requirements: loader must be a valid, non-NULL GdkPixbufLoader* that has not already been closed.
Must be called after the last write/write_bytes to finish loading.
After a successful close, no further write or write_bytes calls should be made on the loader.
On FALSE, error (if non-NULL) is set; callers should not continue writing and should handle cleanup.
error may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should point to a location initialized to NULL and will be set on failure.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_loader_get_format
functions.description: Returns the GdkPixbufFormat corresponding to the image being loaded, or NULL if the format has not yet been determined. Useful for inspecting image properties during incremental loading.
requirements: loader must be a valid, non-NULL GdkPixbufLoader*.
May return NULL until sufficient data has been provided to determine the format.
The returned GdkPixbufFormat is owned by the library; do not free it.

functions.name: gdk_pixdata_serialize
functions.description: Serializes a GdkPixdata into a flat byte stream in network byte order (htonl of struct members followed by pixel_data). Typically used to embed or store pixbuf data as a binary blob. Deprecated since 2.32.
requirements: pixdata must be a valid, initialized GdkPixdata describing pixel data (magic should be GDK_PIXBUF_MAGIC_NUMBER, length either <1 to disable checks or equal to header+payload, types/width/encoding consistent).
If stream_length_p is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory where the resulting stream length will be stored.
Returned buffer is heap-allocated; the caller must free it with g_free when no longer needed.
Only 8-bit samples and RGB/RGBA color types are supported by GdkPixdata (per enum definitions).
The pixel data inside pixdata must be laid out consistently with width, height, and rowstride.

functions.name: gdk_pixdata_deserialize
functions.signature: gboolean gdk_pixdata_deserialize (GdkPixdata *pixdata, guint stream_length, const guint8 *stream, GError **error);
functions.description: Parses a serialized GdkPixdata byte stream (in network byte order) into a GdkPixdata structure. On success returns TRUE and fills pixdata; on failure returns FALSE and sets a GError. Deprecated since 2.32.
requirements: pixdata must be a non-NULL pointer to a GdkPixdata struct to be filled.
stream must point to a buffer of at least stream_length bytes containing a valid serialized GdkPixdata (htonl of members followed by pixel data).
stream_length must be large enough to contain at least GDK_PIXDATA_HEADER_LENGTH and any declared pixel_data payload; otherwise the function will fail.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry; on failure it will be set.

On success, fields of pixdata (including pixel_data, type, dimensions, rowstride) are set to describe the deserialized data; callers should treat the resulting pointers and sizes as owned by pixdata per the implementation’s conventions.
Only encodings and sample widths defined by GdkPixdataType are accepted (RGB/RGBA, 8-bit samples, RAW or RLE).

functions.name: gdk_pixdata_from_pixbuf
functions.signature: gpointer gdk_pixdata_from_pixbuf (GdkPixdata *pixdata, const GdkPixbuf *pixbuf, gboolean use_rle);
functions.description: Converts a GdkPixbuf into a GdkPixdata description, optionally run-length encoding the pixel data. Returns a pointer to the pixel data buffer associated with pixdata for convenience. Deprecated since 2.32.
requirements: pixdata must be a non-NULL pointer to a GdkPixdata struct that will be initialized/filled by this function.
pixbuf must be a non-NULL GdkPixbuf with 8 bits per sample and RGB or RGBA format (alpha optional).
If use_rle is TRUE, the pixel data will be stored with GDK_PIXDATA_ENCODING_RLE; otherwise GDK_PIXDATA_ENCODING_RAW.

The returned gpointer is a heap-allocated buffer holding the serialized pixel payload corresponding to pixdata->pixel_data; the caller is responsible for freeing it with g_free when no longer needed (per typical GLib allocation conventions).
Dimensions, rowstride, and type fields in pixdata will be set to match pixbuf; callers must not modify them arbitrarily.

functions.name: gdk_pixbuf_from_pixdata
functions.signature: GdkPixbuf* gdk_pixbuf_from_pixdata (const GdkPixdata *pixdata, gboolean copy_pixels, GError **error);
functions.description: Creates a GdkPixbuf from a GdkPixdata description. If copy_pixels is TRUE, pixel data is copied; otherwise the pixbuf will reference the existing pixel data. On failure returns NULL and sets a GError. Deprecated since 2.32.
requirements: pixdata must point to a valid, fully-initialized GdkPixdata with correct magic, dimensions, rowstride, type and encoding (RGB or RGBA; 8-bit samples; RAW or RLE).
If copy_pixels is FALSE, pixdata->pixel_data must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the returned GdkPixbuf; the caller retains ownership and must ensure its lifetime outlives the pixbuf.
If copy_pixels is TRUE, sufficient memory must be available to allocate and copy the pixel buffer; the returned pixbuf owns its internal copy.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry; on failure it will be set and the function returns NULL.
Rowstride, width, height, and bytes-per-pixel implied by pixdata must be consistent; otherwise creation will fail.

functions.name: gdk_pixdata_to_csource
functions.signature: GString* gdk_pixdata_to_csource (GdkPixdata *pixdata, const gchar *name, GdkPixdataDumpType dump_type);
functions.description: Generates a GString containing C source representation of the given pixdata. The form of the generated code is controlled by dump_type flags (stream, struct, macros; C vs GLib types; static/const; optional RLE decoder macro). Deprecated since 2.32.
requirements: pixdata must be a valid, initialized GdkPixdata and should describe the image to be emitted.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import Tuple

# This generator creates valid raster image files supported by gdk-pixbuf.
# It focuses on small, well-formed PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, and PPM (PNM) images
# with varying dimensions and properties to exercise different loader paths and
# downscaling options used by the fuzzers. Outputs are <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# -------------------- Helpers --------------------

def _rand(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def _clamp_size(w: int, h: int, bpp: int, overhead: int = 256) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Ensure the resulting file remains under MAX_SIZE; reduce dims if necessary.
    # For conservative bound use w*h*bpp + overhead
    max_pixels = max(1, (MAX_SIZE - overhead) // max(1, bpp))
    area = w * h
    if area <= max_pixels:
        return w, h
    # scale down preserving aspect ratio roughly
    scale = (max_pixels / area) ** 0.5
    w2 = max(1, int(w * scale))
    h2 = max(1, int(h * scale))
    return w2, h2

# -------------------- PNG generator --------------------
# Minimal PNG encoder for 8-bit RGB/RGBA/Gray using uncompressed DEFLATE blocks.
# We craft a valid PNG with IHDR, IDAT (stored blocks), IEND.

def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    import binascii
    return binascii.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _png_chunk(typ: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + typ + data + struct.pack(">I", _crc32(typ + data))


def _zlib_uncompressed(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Build a minimal zlib stream with a single uncompressed deflate block (BTYPE=00)
    # zlib header: CMF/FLG for deflate with 32K window, no dict, checksum correct
    # We'll compute Adler-32 for the payload.
    import zlib
    adler = zlib.adler32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    # Deflate uncompressed blocks must be split into <= 65535 bytes blocks.
    blocks = []
    i = 0
    n = len(data)
    first = True
    while i < n:
        chunk = data[i:i+65535]
        i += len(chunk)
        bfinal = 1 if i >= n else 0
        # BTYPE=00, header 3 bits; we write as byte-packed: [BFINAL|BTYPE=00]
        # Then LEN and NLEN (little-endian 16-bit), followed by raw bytes.
        blocks.append(bytes([bfinal]))
        blocks.append(struct.pack("<H", len(chunk)))
        blocks.append(struct.pack("<H", 0xFFFF - len(chunk)))
        blocks.append(chunk)
    # zlib header: CMF=0x78 (deflate, 32K), FLG computed for no preset dict and FCHECK
    # Choose default 0x9C (fast) or 0x01; use 0x9C commonly used (FCHECK makes header %31 == 0)
    # We'll compute FLG properly: start with FLEVEL=2 (0x80), FDICT=0, set FCHECK.
    CMF = 0x78
    FLG = 0x01  # make simple and recompute FCHECK to satisfy (CMF*256+FLG) % 31 == 0
    for flg in range(256):
        if ((CMF << 8) + flg) % 31 == 0:
            FLG = flg
            break
    z = bytes([CMF, FLG]) + b"".join(blocks) + struct.pack(">I", adler)
    return z


def _png_generate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    color_type = rng.choice([2, 6, 0])  # RGB, RGBA, Gray
    bit_depth = 8
    # Choose dimensions small to keep size tiny; allow variety to trigger scaling paths
    w = _rand(rng, 1, 64)
    h = _rand(rng, 1, 64)
    if color_type == 2:
        bpp = 3
    elif color_type == 6:
        bpp = 4
    else:
        bpp = 1
    w, h = _clamp_size(w, h, bpp + 1, overhead=200)

    # Create raw image data with PNG scanline filter bytes (0 = none) per row
    rows = []
    for y in range(h):
        # generate simple gradients/patterns to increase compressibility variety
        if color_type == 0:
            row = bytes(((x + y) % 256 for x in range(w)))
        elif color_type == 2:
            row = bytes(((x * 3) % 256 for x in range(w))) + \
                  bytes((((x + y) * 5) % 256 for x in range(w)))[:w] + \
                  bytes((((y * 7) + x) % 256 for x in range(w)))
            row = row[:w*3]
        else:  # RGBA
            rgb = bytearray()
            for x in range(w):
                rgb += bytes([(x*5) & 0xFF, (y*3) & 0xFF, ((x+y)*11) & 0xFF])
            alpha = bytes((255 if ((x//4 + y//4) % 2 == 0) else 64) for x in range(w))
            row = bytes(rgb) + alpha
        rows.append(b"\x00" + row)  # filter type 0
    raw = b"".join(rows)
    comp = _zlib_uncompressed(raw)

    sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, bit_depth, color_type, 0, 0, 0)
    data = sig + _png_chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr) + _png_chunk(b"IDAT", comp) + _png_chunk(b"IEND", b"")
    return data

# -------------------- GIF generator --------------------

def _gif_generate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    w = _rand(rng, 1, 64)
    h = _rand(rng, 1, 64)
    w, h = _clamp_size(w, h, 1, overhead=64)
    # Global color table size: 2^(N+1). Choose 4 or 8 colors
    nbits = rng.choice([1, 2, 3])  # 2,4,8 colors
    gct_size = 2 ** (nbits + 1)
    # Build palette
    palette = bytearray()
    for i in range(gct_size):
        palette += bytes([(i*70) % 256, (i*130) % 256, (255 - i*30) % 256])
    # Logical Screen Descriptor
    lsd = struct.pack("<HHBHB", w, h, 0x80 | ((nbits & 0x07) << 0) | ((nbits & 0x07) << 4), 0, 0)
    # Image Descriptor
    idesc = b"\x2C" + struct.pack("<HHHHB", 0, 0, w, h, 0)
    # Minimal LZW image data: create a simple checker index pattern
    # Use LZW min code size = max(2, nbits+1)
    lzw_min = max(2, nbits + 1)
    # Build a trivial sub-block stream with clear/end codes and few indices
    clear = 1 << lzw_min
    end = clear + 1
    # For simplicity, provide a minimal series of codes that many decoders accept: clear, a few indices, end.
    indices = [i % gct_size for i in range(max(1, w*h // 16))]
    codes = [clear] + indices + [end]

    # Pack codes into bytes with initial code size = lzw_min+1 and no growth for simplicity (valid for tiny streams)
    code_size = lzw_min + 1
    bitbuf = 0
    bitlen = 0
    out = bytearray()
    for c in codes:
        bitbuf |= (c & ((1 << 12) - 1)) << bitlen
        bitlen += code_size
        while bitlen >= 8:
            out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)
            bitbuf >>= 8
            bitlen -= 8
    if bitlen:
        out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)
    # Wrap in sub-blocks (size-prefixed, terminated by 0)
    sub = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < len(out):
        chunk = out[i:i+255]
        sub.append(len(chunk))
        sub += chunk
        i += len(chunk)
    sub.append(0)

    data = bytearray()
    data += b"GIF89a"
    data += lsd
    data += palette
    data += idesc
    data += bytes([lzw_min])
    data += sub
    data += b"\x3B"  # trailer
    return bytes(data)

# -------------------- BMP generator --------------------

def _bmp_generate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 24-bit BMP with no compression, bottom-up
    w = _rand(rng, 1, 64)
    h = _rand(rng, 1, 64)
    # Row padding to multiple of 4 bytes
    row_bytes = (w * 3 + 3) & ~3
    w, h = _clamp_size(w, h, row_bytes, overhead=54)
    row_bytes = (w * 3 + 3) & ~3
    pixel_data = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        row = bytearray()
        for x in range(w):
            # B, G, R
            row += bytes([((x*11) & 0xFF), ((y*7) & 0xFF), (((x+y)*5) & 0xFF)])
        row += b"\x00" * (row_bytes - 3*w)
        pixel_data[:0]  # no-op
        pixel_data = pixel_data  # to keep linters happy
        # BMP bottom-up: append from bottom row first; we will build after generating all rows
    rows = []
    for y in range(h):
        row = bytearray()
        for x in range(w):
            row += bytes([((x*11) & 0xFF), ((y*7) & 0xFF), (((x+y)*5) & 0xFF)])
        row += b"\x00" * (row_bytes - 3*w)
        rows.append(bytes(row))
    pixel_bytes = b"".join(reversed(rows))
    bfType = b"BM"
    bfOffBits = 14 + 40  # headers
    bfSize = bfOffBits + len(pixel_bytes)
    file_hdr = bfType + struct.pack("<IHHI", bfSize, 0, 0, bfOffBits)
    info_hdr = struct.pack("<IIIHHIIIIII", 40, w, h, 1, 24, 0, len(pixel_bytes), 2835, 2835, 0, 0)
    return file_hdr + info_hdr + pixel_bytes

# -------------------- PPM (P6) generator --------------------

def _ppm_generate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Binary PPM: P6\nW H\n255\n + raw RGB
    w = _rand(rng, 1, 96)
    h = _rand(rng, 1, 96)
    w, h = _clamp_size(w, h, 3, overhead=32)
    header = f"P6\n{w} {h}\n255\n".encode("ascii")
    rgb = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            rgb += bytes([(x*3) & 0xFF, (y*5) & 0xFF, ((x+y)*11) & 0xFF])
    return header + bytes(rgb)

# -------------------- JPEG generator --------------------
# Minimal baseline JPEG encoder is complex; instead we construct a tiny valid JFIF
# by leveraging a precomputed minimal image and patching quantization/size a bit.

_MIN_JPEG = (
    b"\xFF\xD8"  # SOI
    b"\xFF\xE0\x00\x10JFIF\x00\x01\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00"  # APP0 JFIF
    b"\xFF\xDB\x00C\x00" + bytes([
        16,11,12,14,12,10,16,14,13,14,18,16,16,18,23,37,25,23,21,21,23,46,33,35,28,37,55,48,58,57,54,48,53,52,61,69,88,74,61,64,84,65,52,53,76,103,77,84,89,92,98,99,98,60,74,109,116,108,95,115,87,96,98,96
    ]) +
    b"\xFF\xC0\x00\x11\x08\x00\x01\x00\x01\x03\x01\x11\x00\x02\x11\x01\x03\x11\x01"  # SOF0 1x1, 3 components
    b"\xFF\xC4\x00\x14\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00"  # minimal DC table
    b"\xFF\xDA\x00\x0C\x03\x01\x00\x02\x00\x03\x00\x00\x3F\x00"  # SOS
    b"\x00"  # minimal entropy data
    b"\xFF\xD9"
)


def _jpeg_generate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Provide the minimal valid JPEG; gdk-pixbuf will accept and then scaling paths will exercise code.
    # Randomly duplicate some APP0/COM segments to vary a little but keep validity.
    data = bytearray(_MIN_JPEG)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        com = b"\xFF\xFE" + struct.pack(">H", 2 + 8) + b"fuzzJPEG"
        # Inject after SOI
        data = bytearray(b"\xFF\xD8" + com + bytes(data[2:]))
    return bytes(data)

# -------------------- Main selection --------------------

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    gen = rng.choices(
        population=[_png_generate, _gif_generate, _bmp_generate, _ppm_generate, _jpeg_generate],
        weights=[35, 20, 20, 15, 10],
        k=1,
    )[0]
    blob = gen(rng)
    if len(blob) > MAX_SIZE:
        # As a last resort, truncate only for formats that tolerate it (PPM, BMP would not; PNG/JPEG/GIF would break).
        # Instead, if oversized, regenerate with PNG tiny 1x1 to ensure validity under cap.
        blob = _png_generate(rng)
        if len(blob) > MAX_SIZE:
            blob = blob[:MAX_SIZE]
    return blob

import os
